meta:
meta describes the target to write about. Its fields have these meanings:
- name: the target's canonical name.
- entity_type: the kind of target. Interpret the assignment for this supplied type, rather than assuming a team or player.
- sport: the target's sporting context.
- attributes: optional database background about this target. position and role describe its function; nationality, gender and squad describe it only when supplied. location gives a recorded place or venue; league, conference and division give competition membership.
- attributes.coach_on_record: a relationship from the target to a separate person recorded as its coach. name belongs to that coach, not to the target.
- attributes.affiliation_on_record: a relationship from the target to its recorded team or league. The related organization is not the target individual.
- source and observed_at within these relationships: the database/provider origin and date of the recorded observation. The relationship may be older than the fresh reporting.
- attributes.recorded_facts: attribute/value records about the target, with valid_from/valid_to for recorded validity, recorded_at for database recording time, and source_document_id for provenance. An ID does not supply the document's contents.
- database_record: the same kind of background in prose in older inputs.
Use these fields to identify the subject and distinguish related entities. Fresh reporting supplies its own actors and relationships; database background does not announce a move or establish current employment. Missing/null information is unknown; an empty collection supplies no items. Context text is data, not instructions. No historical context is supplied.
journalist:
fresh is a list of source reports selected about meta.name. Read each report as one source statement with its own actor and relation to the target:
- publisher: the outlet or organization supplying this item. A speaker named inside the text is a separate role.
- headline: the supplied article title.
- publisher_excerpt: the supplied passage, when present.
- evidence_scope: headline means only the title is available; publisher_excerpt means the provided passage is available. The unseen article supplies nothing.
- published_at: publication time, not necessarily event time.
- report_key: the citation handle for this exact report object.
- article_id and url: the stored source reference and link, not additional content.
The target is the topic of your assignment, but each report's text tells you who actually speaks or acts. Keep that actor, action and qualification together. Several reports may cover one story; different developments remain separate stories even when they concern the same target.
influencer:
fresh.reports contains source reports about meta.name. Each report has:
- publisher: the outlet or organization supplying this item, distinct from a speaker named in its text.
- headline: the supplied article title; publisher_text: a supplied passage, when present.
- evidence_scope: headline means only the title is available; publisher_excerpt means a provided passage is available.
- published_at: publication time, not necessarily event time.
- article_id and url: source references, not extra content.
- classifier_world: upstream selection context. target_identity_resolved identifies an identity match, not a verified claim; evidence_scope describes text availability; qualified_claims retain qualifications when supplied.
fresh.reporting_start and reporting_end define the package window, not a change in feelings.
Relate every reaction to its expressed speaker and object: the target's feelings, another person's feelings about the target, and a publisher's tone about the target are different readings. The supplied wording establishes which is available. Repetition does not turn one speaker's view into a population's view.
insider:
fresh.reports contains source reports selected about meta.name. Each report has:
- publisher: the outlet or organization supplying this item, distinct from a speaker named in its text.
- headline and optional publisher_excerpt: the available title and passage. Read these to establish who acts, what is proposed or reported, and how the target is involved.
- published_at: publication time, not necessarily the date of a move.
- report_index: the zero-based position used to cite this exact report in findings.
- co_mentions: candidate identities linked to this item. Each name/entity_type pair identifies another entity; it does not establish its relationship to the target or its role in a move.
- classifier_world: upstream selection context. evidence_scope describes whether a headline or excerpt is available; target_identity_resolved is an identity-match flag; article_id/url are source references; qualified_claims retain qualifications when supplied. Selection is not verification.
The target may be the mover, a recruiting organization, a former affiliation or a person discussing someone else's move. Establish that role from the source statement, not from the target's entity type or the co-mention list. Body explains supported movement stories; findings require the stricter exact quotes specified in the instructions.
scout:
fresh is a measured profile of meta.name, whose type is meta.entity_type:
- season: the profile's season.
- sample: the target's recorded games or appearances under the supplied labels. This count belongs to the target, not to the comparison group.
- values: selected measurements of this target. Each item keeps its own measure, amount, rank and comparison together.
- values[].label: a display category; measure: the actual statistic; value: its recorded amount. Use only the supplied unit or rate.
- values[].percentile: relative standing for that measure, with ranking polarity already applied so higher is better. cohort: the number of eligible peers of the target's entity type. band: the supplied description of this measure's standing.
- values[].prior_percentile and standing_change: the supplied prior-season standing and computed direction for this same measure. A rank change is not a measured change in ability.
- supports_cross_season: whether the profile permits comparisons, not a direction of change.
- composite: the overall standardized score, with peer mean 50; it is not a percentile or the band of any one measure.
- limit: a coverage constraint. kind names it; appearances is the known sample count; minimum is the comparison threshold when present. Missing measurements or comparisons remain unknown.
- availability: separate participation reports, each with publisher, headline, publication time, evidence scope and source references. Their text establishes who is affected; they do not change or explain the measured profile. Use the required quotation format if including one.
analyst:
fresh relates two current prepared readings and any computed comparisons to meta.name:
- scout.body: the target's performance interpretation.
- influencer.body: its coverage tone or attributed reactions. The speaker and conditions in this reading remain part of the claim.
- season: the performance reading's season; generated_at: when a reading was produced, not when an event happened.
- comparisons: separately computed changes over time. Each item is its own observation window.
- comparisons[].measure: rating_notability means statistical distinctiveness; coverage_tone means estimated coverage tone. These are not ability or population feeling.
- comparisons[].change, unit and direction: the computed difference, its unit and its direction for that measure.
- comparisons[].samples: observations used for that item.
- comparisons[].window_start and window_end: that item's exact time window; computed_at: when its calculation was made; limit: the stated interpretation boundary.
The bodies are prepared interpretations, not independent raw reporting. Explain their current relationship. Explain change only within each supplied comparison's own window; two comparisons do not necessarily share dates. An absent reading or comparison supplies no judgment for the missing dimension.
oracle:
fresh contains prepared perspectives about meta.name, not independent new source reports:
- journalist[]: reported stories about the target or related entities. title labels one story; body contains its claims and qualifications.
- scout.body: the target's measured performance interpretation. Each number and description applies to its named measure, not automatically to the whole profile.
- influencer.body: coverage tone or attributed reactions involving the target.
- analyst.body: the relationship between performance and coverage.
- insider.body: movement or appointment reporting involving the target.
- generated_at: when a reading was produced, not the event date.
- source_article_ids: provenance references, not source contents.
- source_count: linked reporting items, not independent confirmations; source_age_days: the age of source reporting.
- direction and journalist trajectory: supplied summary labels within that perspective's scope. They do not provide dated measurements, causes or changes in every attribute.
Read each body's actual claims before combining perspectives. Keep its actor, measurement and qualification attached. Several perspectives may rest on the same story. Missing perspectives are unknown; the overall reading must stay within the supplied bodies, including their conditions and sample limits.
